paper_title: Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs
core_problem: Large language models struggle to effectively use tools via API calls, generating inaccurate input arguments and hallucinating wrong API usage. Supporting a web-scale collection of potentially millions of changing APIs with overlapping functionality and nuanced constraints cannot be described in a single context, requiring new integration approaches and benchmarks for tool use.
methodology_summary: A LLaMA-based model is instruction fine-tuned to enhance API call generation, with a first study of fine-tuning a base model supplemented by information retrieval. The approach emphasizes tool use over conversational refinement and is combined with a document retriever to provide up-to-date API documentation at test time, enabling adaptation to test-time document changes, user updates and version changes.
datasets_eval: APIBench, a comprehensive dataset consisting of HuggingFace, TorchHub and TensorHub APIs, introduced to evaluate API call writing ability and hallucination.
empirical_results: Gorilla surpasses GPT-4 on writing API calls. When combined with a document retriever it demonstrates strong capability to adapt to test-time document changes and substantially mitigates hallucination commonly encountered when prompting LLMs directly. Evaluation shows improved accuracy versus hallucination across settings.
explicit_limitations: No explicit limitations are provided in the given context.
